justification: Assessment returned INVALID and localized the flaw to the |R_{m-1}| < n/2 case: padding R_{m-1} up to size n/2 inside W_{m-1} and then asserting the padded S still has no neighbor in W_m 'since S ⊇ R_{m-1}'. That is verbatim the ground-truth flaw (non-monotone property inherited upward to a superset; padding vertices are unreachable from W_1 but unconstrained in adjacency to W_m), including the same downstream consequences (N(S) ⊆ V \ W_m and |N(S)| ≤ αn unjustified, no contradiction). Its witness differs from the ground-truth one (n=8, α=1/8, K_7 on {2..8} plus pendant edge {1,2}, W_{m-1}=W_m={1,3,...,8}, R={1}, S={1,3,4,5}) but is a valid witness for the same claim: N({1})={2} ∉ W_m so R has no neighbor in W_m, while N(S)={2,...,8} meets W_m in {3,...,8}, and every 4-set S with {1} ⊆ S ⊆ W_{m-1} contains clique vertices, so all admissible paddings fail. Expansion |N(T)| ≥ n/2 + αn = 5 for all |T| = 4 checks out since any 4-set touches the K_7 and hence N(T) ⊇ {2,...,8}. Different-but-valid witness for the identical defect counts as matching.
